name: The Great Pyramid of Giza
scope: The last surviving wonder of the ancient world, on the Giza plateau outside Cairo, built for Pharaoh Khufu (~2560 BC). T1: it is the ONLY one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still standing today. T2: at 146.6 m it was the tallest human-made structure on Earth for more than 3,800 years, from ~2560 BC until a cathedral spire finally topped it around AD 1311 (invert the wonder: 'for 38 centuries nothing built was taller' -> the Great Pyramid). T3: its four sides are aligned to true north, south, east and west to within about a tenth of a degree (3 arc-minutes) -- more precisely than most modern buildings. T4: it is built of about 2.3 million limestone blocks, and the King's Chamber is roofed with granite beams hauled ~800 km down the Nile from Aswan, the largest weighing ~80 tonnes. T5: narrow 'star shafts' angle up from the chambers; around 2500 BC one pointed toward the northern pole-star region and one toward Orion's belt (the god Osiris) -- a much-argued sky-alignment. Extra rungs: the original smooth white Tura-limestone casing (later stripped for Cairo's buildings); the shifting entrance and Grand Gallery; ~20 years of organized labor by paid work-gangs (not slaves), whose graffiti names survive.

name: The Great Sphinx of Giza
scope: The lion-bodied, human-headed guardian of the Giza plateau. T1: unlike the block-built pyramids beside it, the Sphinx was carved from ONE single mass of natural limestone bedrock -- the largest monolith statue on Earth. T2: it faces due EAST, staring straight at the point where the sun rises. T3: at 73 m long and 20 m high it is the oldest known monumental sculpture in Egypt (~2500 BC, Old Kingdom). T4: the human face is thought to be Pharaoh Khafre; its nose has been missing for centuries -- and a 1737 drawing already shows it gone, so Napoleon's soldiers did NOT knock it off (a famous myth), the damage was likely deliberate around the 14th century. T5: a fringe 'water-erosion hypothesis' (geologist Robert Schoch) claims the deep weathering grooves on the enclosure walls were cut by heavy RAIN, implying a far older date -- a claim mainstream geology rejects as pseudo-archaeology.

name: Karnak & ancient Thebes (Luxor)
scope: The largest religious building complex ever constructed, at ancient Thebes (modern Luxor) on the Nile. T1: Karnak's Precinct of Amun-Re is so vast that St. Peter's, Notre-Dame, and Milan Cathedral could all fit inside it -- it is the biggest temple ever built. T2: its Great Hypostyle Hall is a stone FOREST of 134 giant columns; the 12 central ones stand 21 m tall (a 6-7 story building) and you walk among them like tree-trunks. T3: about 30 different pharaohs added to Karnak across ~2,000 years -- it was never 'finished,' each king building onto the last. T4: a 3 km avenue of ram-headed sphinxes (the ram = the god Amun) once linked Karnak to Luxor Temple, and has now been re-excavated and reopened as the 'Avenue of Sphinxes.' T5: the hall's columns are shaped like papyrus and lotus stalks and topped with 70-tonne stone architraves that once held a roof -- turning the hall into a symbolic stone marsh. Extra rungs: the sacred lake; Hatshepsut's red-granite obelisk (the tallest ancient obelisk still standing in Egypt, ~29 m); the Egyptian name Ipet-isut, 'the Most Select of Places.'

name: Abu Simbel
scope: Ramesses II's rock-cut temple in far southern Egypt, and its extraordinary 1960s rescue. T1: the temple front is guarded by four SEATED colossi of Ramesses II, each carved 20 m tall (a 6-story building) straight out of a sandstone cliff. T2: in the 1960s the new Aswan High Dam was about to drown the whole temple under Lake Nasser -- so an international team SAWED it into 1,036 numbered blocks and rebuilt it on higher ground. T3: the temple was lifted 65 m higher and moved ~208 m back from the water, reassembled so precisely you can barely find the seams. T4: it was carved so that TWICE a year -- February 22 and October 22 -- the dawn sun shoots ~60 m down the corridor and lights the faces of three gods on the back wall, while Ptah, god of the underworld, stays in shadow. T5: even after the move the sun-alignment still works, just shifted by about a day -- modern engineers couldn't perfectly reproduce the 3,200-year-old astronomy.

name: The Nile
scope: The river that made Egypt possible -- a green ribbon of life across the Sahara. T1: Egypt is almost entirely desert, yet a thin strip of farmland runs its whole length, because the Nile flows right across it; the Greek Herodotus called Egypt 'the gift of the Nile.' T2: unusually, the Nile flows NORTH -- from the highlands of the south down to the Mediterranean -- which is why 'Upper Egypt' is in the south (upstream) and 'Lower Egypt' is the northern delta. T3: every summer the Nile used to FLOOD, spreading black fertile mud over the fields; the Egyptians named their land Kemet, 'the Black Land,' for that dark soil (the red desert beyond was Deshret, 'the Red Land'). T4: the flood came from the Blue Nile, born in the Ethiopian highlands, which dumps summer-monsoon rain into the river, while the White Nile from Lake Victoria keeps it flowing all year -- the two meet at Khartoum. T5: at ~6,650 km the Nile is traditionally counted the longest river on Earth (a title it trades with the Amazon); at its mouth it splits into the triangular Nile Delta, the fan shape that gave the Greek letter delta its name. Extra rung: since the Aswan High Dam (1970) the flood no longer comes -- the silt is trapped in Lake Nasser, so the delta is now shrinking and eroding into the sea, and farmers rely on fertilizer instead of the river's mud.

name: Petra
scope: A whole city carved into rose-red sandstone cliffs in a desert gorge in Jordan, capital of the Nabataeans. T1: Petra's famous facade, Al-Khazneh ('the Treasury'), is cut ~40 m up into a solid rock wall -- a temple-front sculpted out of the living cliff, not built from blocks. T2: you reach it by walking through the Siq, a natural crack in the rock over 1 km long and in places only 3-4 m wide, with cliffs ~100 m overhead -- then the Treasury suddenly blazes into view in the gap. T3: the 'Treasury' isn't a treasury at all -- it's a monumental TOMB (probably of the Nabataean king Aretas IV); its name comes from a legend that a pharaoh hid gold inside the stone urn carved at the top. T4: Petra should have been impossible -- a city of ~20,000 people in a bone-dry gorge -- but the Nabataeans engineered dams, rock-cut channels, and cisterns that trapped every flash flood and piped water through the whole city, even selling the surplus. T5: the largest monument is Ad-Deir, 'the Monastery,' ~45 m tall and carved even higher up the mountain -- an 800-step climb above the valley. Extra rungs: the rose-red banded color comes from iron in the sandstone; the poet John Burgon called it 'a rose-red city half as old as time' (1845); Petra grew rich as a hub of the incense road, taxing caravans of frankincense and myrrh from Arabia; a great earthquake in AD 363 wrecked the water system and helped end the city.

name: Palmyra
scope: A ruined caravan city standing alone in the Syrian desert, the 'bride of the desert.' T1: Palmyra is a field of tall stone colonnades rising straight out of the empty sand -- an entire classical city marooned in the middle of the desert. T2: it exists only because of the Efqa spring, an oasis in the middle of nowhere -- the one reliable water for days in any direction, so every caravan crossing the desert HAD to stop there. T3: Palmyra grew rich by taxing the caravans that carried silk and spices between the Roman Mediterranean and Persia along the Silk Road -- a desert toll-booth that became a metropolis. T4: its most famous ruler was Queen Zenobia, who around AD 270 broke Palmyra away from Rome and briefly ruled an empire reaching to Egypt, before the emperor Aurelian crushed the revolt (~AD 272). T5: in 2015 ISIS deliberately blew up Palmyra's greatest monuments -- the Temple of Bel and the Arch of Triumph -- as an act of cultural destruction; 3D scans made before the war are now guiding the reconstruction.

name: Baalbek
scope: The Roman temple of Jupiter at Baalbek in Lebanon, built on the largest cut stones on Earth. T1: the six surviving columns of the Temple of Jupiter are the tallest of any Roman temple -- each ~20 m high (a 6-story building) -- and they stand on a platform of unbelievably huge stone blocks. T2: three blocks in that platform, the Trilithon, each weigh about 800 tonnes -- heavier than a fully loaded jumbo jet -- and exactly how the Romans dragged and lifted them is still not fully understood. T3: still lying in the nearby quarry is the 'Stone of the Pregnant Woman' (Hajar al-Hibla), a single cut block of ~1,000 tonnes that was never moved. T4: in 2014 archaeologists found an EVEN BIGGER stone beside it -- about 1,650 tonnes -- the largest block ever quarried by human hands anywhere in the world. T5: the Romans called the city Heliopolis, 'City of the Sun,' and its temple was one of the largest in the whole empire -- the megaliths sit UNDER a Roman temple, so the puzzle is Roman engineering, not aliens.

name: Persepolis
scope: The ceremonial capital of the Persian (Achaemenid) Empire, a palace-city on a great stone terrace, begun by Darius I (~515 BC). T1: Persepolis was reached by a grand double staircase so gently sloped that horsemen and dignitaries could ride and walk straight up onto the terrace. T2: its Apadana audience hall was ringed by columns ~20 m tall and astonishingly slender -- Persian columns were far thinner and taller than Greek ones, like stone reeds. T3: the Apadana's stone staircase is carved with a PROCESSION of 23 subject nations, each in its own national dress, bringing tribute-gifts -- Nubians with a giraffe, Armenians with a horse, Bactrians with a camel -- a frozen stone photograph of the whole ancient world. T4: the entrance was the Gate of All Nations, flanked by lamassu -- giant human-headed winged bulls carved as guardians. T5: in 330 BC Alexander the Great burned Persepolis to the ground -- maybe drunk at a victory feast, maybe as deliberate revenge for the Persian burning of Athens -- and the fire baked and preserved thousands of clay record-tablets that survive to this day.

name: Babylon & the Ishtar Gate
scope: The great blue gateway into ancient Babylon, on the Euphrates in Iraq. T1: the Ishtar Gate was a towering entrance faced in glazed bricks the deep blue of lapis lazuli, covered in rows of golden animals -- one of eight gates through Babylon's walls. T2: across the blue walls march relief animals in yellow and brown: bulls for the storm-god Adad, lions for the goddess Ishtar, and a strange dragon called the mushhushshu (the god Marduk's beast) -- a snake-headed, scaly creature with a lion's front legs and an eagle's hind claws. T3: it was built ~575 BC by King Nebuchadnezzar II (the Bible's king of the Babylonian captivity); beyond it ran the grand Processional Way, its walls lined with ~120 striding lions. T4: the surprise is that the gate you can visit today is NOT in Iraq -- German archaeologists dug up the bricks around 1900 and rebuilt the whole ~14 m gate inside the Pergamon Museum in Berlin. T5: Babylon was also home to the legendary Hanging Gardens, one of the Seven Wonders -- but no trace has ever been found, and some scholars think they were really at Nineveh, or never existed at all (label as legend/disputed). Extra rungs: the biblical Tower of Babel likely echoes a real Babylonian ziggurat, Etemenanki, 'the foundation of heaven and earth'; the name Babylon means 'gate of the gods.'

name: Göbekli Tepe
scope: A hilltop ring of giant carved pillars in southern Turkey that rewrote the story of civilization. T1: Göbekli Tepe is a set of circles of huge T-shaped stone pillars, and it is about 11,500 years old -- built roughly 6,000 years before Stonehenge and before the Egyptian pyramids. T2: it was built by HUNTER-GATHERERS -- people who had not yet invented farming, pottery, metal, or writing -- overturning the old assumption that you needed a settled farming town before you could raise a monument. T3: the T-shaped pillars are carved in relief with wild animals -- foxes, boars, snakes, scorpions, vultures, cranes -- a stone bestiary of the late ice age; the tallest pillars stand ~5.5 m and weigh several tonnes each. T4: the pillars seem to be stylized PEOPLE -- some have carved arms folding around to the front, with belts and loincloths -- giant abstract guardians standing shoulder to shoulder in a ring. T5: strangest of all, the builders deliberately BURIED the whole complex under tonnes of rubble when they were done, which is why it survived so intact -- and the site suggests the temple may have come BEFORE the farming town, not after (excavator Klaus Schmidt: 'first came the temple, then the city').

name: Çatalhöyük
scope: A 9,000-year-old Neolithic proto-town in central Turkey. T1: Catalhoyuk had NO streets and NO doors at ground level -- its mud-brick houses were packed wall-to-wall like a honeycomb, and you entered your own house through a hole in the ROOF, climbing down a ladder. T2: the people buried their DEAD right inside the home -- under the floors and sleeping platforms -- so each family lived directly above its own ancestors. T3: one of its wall paintings is often called the world's oldest MAP: a town-plan with a twin-peaked volcano (Hasan Dag) erupting behind it, painted ~8,600 years ago -- though some scholars argue it is really a leopard skin and a geometric pattern, not a map at all (label as disputed).

name: Cappadocia & the Derinkuyu underground cities
scope: A volcanic dreamscape in central Turkey where people carved whole cities out of soft rock, above ground and below. T1: in Cappadocia wind and water have eroded soft volcanic rock into a valley of 'fairy chimneys' -- tall stone cones and mushroom-shaped pillars, each capped by a harder boulder that shields the softer rock beneath it. T2: because the rock (tuff, hardened volcanic ash) is soft enough to dig with hand tools but hardens on exposure to air, people carved their HOUSES, churches, and stables straight into the cones and cliffs. T3: they also dug DOWN -- Derinkuyu is a whole underground city cut ~85 m deep (like an 18-story building, but downward) with room for as many as 20,000 people plus their livestock and food stores. T4: to seal it against raiders, each level could be blocked by huge round stone DOORS, like millstones, rolled across the passage from the INSIDE -- so attackers couldn't open them. T5: it stayed livable because of a hidden network of ventilation shafts (one ~55 m deep also served as a well) that pulled fresh air down to the lowest floors, and Derinkuyu even connected to another underground city, Kaymakli, through ~9 km of tunnels. Extra rung: the whole city was forgotten for centuries -- rediscovered only in 1963, when a man knocking down a wall in his basement found a passage leading into it.

name: The Dead Sea
scope: The lowest, saltiest lake on Earth, in the Jordan Rift Valley between Israel and Jordan. T1: the shore of the Dead Sea is the LOWEST dry land on the planet -- about 430 m below sea level -- there is nowhere on Earth's land surface you can stand lower, and it is still dropping. T2: it is called 'dead' because almost nothing lives in it: the water is roughly 34% salt, nearly TEN times saltier than the ocean, far too salty for fish or plants. T3: the water is so dense with dissolved salt that a person cannot sink -- bathers famously FLOAT on the surface, able to lie back and read a newspaper. T4: it is a 'dead end' for water -- the Jordan River flows IN but nothing flows OUT (an endorheic basin), so water leaves only by evaporating in the desert heat, and that is exactly what concentrates all the salt. T5: along the shore, salt crystallizes into eerie white pillars and towers -- Mount Sodom is an entire hill of rock salt -- and the biblical story of Lot's wife turning to a pillar of salt is set right here (named as a place-legend). Extra rung: the sea is shrinking fast -- as Israel and Jordan divert the Jordan River, the water drops ~1 m a year and the retreating shore is collapsing into thousands of dangerous sinkholes.

Accuracy rail: ~430 m below sea level (lowest land on Earth), ~34% salinity (~9-10x the ocean), endorheic -- TEACH 'endorheic' (a basin with no outlet) before testing it; the shrinkage and sinkholes are real and current. Distractors = other real salt/superlative water bodies (Utah's Great Salt Lake, the Caspian, Lake Assal, Baikal). Lane border: this is a NATURAL wonder -- keep answers on the geology and chemistry (elevation, salinity, density/buoyancy, endorheic basin, salt pillars, sinkholes), not the Dead Sea Scrolls (history).
